newsitem.title: FRANCE: Brigitte Bardot appeals to Australia on sheep.
newsitem.headline: Brigitte Bardot appeals to Australia on sheep.

text.p: Film star turned animal rights champion Brigitte Bardot has called on Australia to halt live sheep exports to Arab Middle East states, saying the animals suffered aboard "concentration camp-like ships."
Bardot made the appeal in a letter sent this week to Australian Prime Minister John Howard which was released to media in Paris on Friday.

"Can you not transport carcasses and thus prevent more than 500 hours suffering to each of these sheep raised on the open range and which find themselves callously thrown onto concentration camp-like ships for their last voyage to a horrible destiny," Bardot said.
The ex-actress's letter was accompanied by stark photos of sheep, some apparently ill, disembarking from a vessel arriving from Australia in the United Arab Emirates.

Bardot, who said the sheep later had their throats slit without being stunned, made no mention in the letter of her years-old campaign against the Moslem ritual slaughter of sheep during the Eid el-Kabir festival.
Bardot, 62, appeared in court last month where she was cleared of inciting racial hatred over statements she made in criticising the festival.
